title: The Burning Thorn
premise: Jonah Eriksen has spent years making themselves unremarkable: a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons, and a smuggler who knows every goat-track through the Thornfell mountains. But when their lover, the cartographer Wren, finds Jonah's face and tonight's date inked in a century-old book of prophecies, invisibility becomes impossible. The prophecy names them the 'thorn that burns'—the one fated to descend into the court beneath the mountain and steal back the soul of Alaric Vane, a prince sold to the deep court a hundred years ago in exchange for an endless winter's protection. Hunted by the crown, betrayed by the guild that trained them, and falling deeper in love with Wren even as duty demands they go alone, Jonah must choose between the safety of being no one and the terrible weight of inheritance. In the end, Jonah reclaims not only Alaric's soul but their own stolen history—the Eriksen family were the original sellers—and breaks the winter by paying the debt with memory instead of blood, returning changed to a spring thaw and a life chosen rather than assigned.
about_author: Marguerite Amberdale is the pen name of a former pastry chef who spent a decade working in castle-adjacent hotels before turning to fantasy. She writes about food, borders, and the people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A routine day tasting for Queen Isolde establishes Jonah's poisoned immunity, their careful anonymity, and their secret evening meeting with Wren. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine built on quiet self-erasure.

chapters.title: A Date With Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the archive, Wren cross-references an old prophecy book for a commission and finds Jonah's face sketched beside tomorrow's date. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Thornfell Roads
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah walks Wren through the smuggler paths they know by heart, explaining how goods—and people—move unseen beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared secrets of the land.

chapters.title: What the Prophecy Promises
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The full prophecy is read aloud: a thorn that burns will steal back what was sold before the long winter finishes falling. Wren realizes 'the long winter' may be literal. Emotional beat: reluctant belief.

chapters.title: The Queen's Suspicion
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Queen Isolde summons Jonah, probing about their family name—erased from records a century ago. Someone at court knows more than they should. Emotional beat: the first crack in Jonah's armor of anonymity.

chapters.title: Alaric Vane, Sold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Archive digging reveals Prince Alaric Vane was traded to the court beneath the mountain one hundred years ago; the endless winter is the payment still running. Emotional beat: horror at the cost of the kingdom's comfort.

chapters.title: The Guild Summons
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Smugglers' Guild, which raised Jonah after their parents vanished, orders them to stop asking questions—or be given to whoever asks next. Emotional beat: the family that owns you isn't family.

chapters.title: Wren Draws a Map to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren maps the mountain's underside from fragmentary sources and finds a sealed gate matching Jonah's birthmark-shaped scar. Emotional beat: love expressed as cartography.

chapters.title: Poison Practice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah deliberately doses themselves with a rare venom to build resistance for what's coming, nearly dying alone. Emotional beat: grim preparation; the body as a weapon forged against oneself.

chapters.title: The First Hunter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A crown inquisitor, Serah Dole, corners Wren, revealing the queen wants the prophecy fulfilled on the crown's terms—with Jonah as expendable bait. Emotional beat: hunted together means endangered together.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Passes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah and Wren flee into the Thornfells ahead of the first true snow, using smuggler roads to shake pursuit. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror entwined on the run.

chapters.title: The Hollow Inn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sheltering at an inn that exists on no map, they meet Old Maret, who remembers the night Alaric was taken—and recognizes Jonah's surname. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Maret's Testimony
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Maret reveals the Eriksens brokered the soul-sale; Jonah's parents died trying to undo it. Jonah inherits both the guilt and the obligation. Emotional beat: grief for parents finally understood.

chapters.title: What Was Sold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The mechanics of the sale: Alaric's soul anchors the winter-pact; the deep court feeds on it nightly. Stealing it back means the kingdom loses its shield. Emotional beat: the moral weight of the theft.

chapters.title: Serah Catches Up
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Serah Dole ambushes them at a bridge; Jonah's poison-honed reflexes save them, but Serah escapes with Wren's map. Emotional beat: fury and fear—their route is compromised.

chapters.title: The False Gate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the stolen map's logic, they realize Serah will open the wrong door and wake something worse. They must beat her to the true gate. Emotional beat: racing against their own mistake.

chapters.title: Down the Goat-Track
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A brutal descent through a storm only Jonah could navigate, carrying an injured Wren. Emotional beat: tenderness under extremity; love as physical labor.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Root
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They find the real gate hidden inside a hollowed ancient thorn-tree—the burning thorn of the prophecy. Emotional beat: awe and dread at standing on the threshold.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Stone
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The gate demands a toll of memory. Jonah pays a small one—a childhood summer—and the door opens. Emotional beat: the first taste of what the journey will cost.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Descent into the deep court: a mirrored inversion of the palace above, lit by cold fire, where courtiers wear borrowed faces. Emotional beat: uncanny beauty masking hunger.

chapters.title: Audience With the Pale Regent
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Pale Regent offers Jonah a bargain: leave with their life, forget everything, and the winter continues peacefully. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable forgetting.

chapters.title: Finding Alaric
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They locate Alaric—not a monster but a man worn thin by a century of being fed upon, barely remembering his own name. Emotional beat: compassion for the forgotten prince.

chapters.title: The Taster's Advantage
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At a deep-court banquet, Jonah's immunity lets them safely eat what would kill any rescuer, buying trust and time among the courtiers. Emotional beat: every scar becoming useful at last.

chapters.title: Serah Below
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Serah arrives via the false gate, half-consumed by what she woke, and bargains her knowledge for passage out. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: enemies bound by shared peril.

chapters.title: The Regent's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Regent reveals the truth: the crown above has always known and always renewed the pact. Jonah's queen would let them die here. Emotional beat: betrayal by the duty they served.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Regent offers Wren a place as court cartographer—immortality, prestige—if they abandon Jonah. Wren refuses. Emotional beat: love declared against immortality's price.

chapters.title: Stealing the Soul
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The heist: using taster's sleight-of-hand, Jonah lifts Alaric's soul—a small burning seed—from the Regent's reliquary during a ceremony. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by alarms rising.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. As they flee upward, the pact begins collapsing; the winter above intensifies catastrophically, exactly as prophesied. The kingdom will blame them. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve intertwined.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Mirrored Halls
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A running battle through the deep court; Serah sacrifices herself to hold the gate, whispering that she once loved someone the crown erased too. Emotional beat: unexpected grace from an enemy.

chapters.title: The Toll Reckoned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the gate, the full toll comes due: the door demands the rest of what Jonah paid toward. Wren offers their own memories of Jonah instead. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the purest form of love.

chapters.title: What Jonah Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah refuses Wren's offer and instead pays with the Eriksen inheritance itself—the ancestral claim that made them the seller's heir, erasing the debt's root. Emotional beat: breaking a cycle by unmaking one's own title.

chapters.title: Alaric's Return
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They surface into blizzard with Alaric's soul-seed intact. Alaric, reviving, remembers his sale and testifies to the crown's century of complicity. Emotional beat: witness as weapon.

chapters.title: The Queen's Judgment
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Brought before Queen Isolde in chains, Jonah presents Alaric alive and the evidence of the pact. The court fractures; the old guard falls. Emotional beat: the invisible made undeniable.

chapters.title: Winter Without a Pact
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The unprotected winter turns lethal; famine looms. Jonah proposes the unthinkable: renegotiate with the deep court openly, as equals, rather than by secret sacrifice. Emotional beat: courage to face what hiding created.

chapters.title: Parley at the Thorn-Door
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah, Wren, and Alaric parley with the Pale Regent: memories freely given in trade, not souls stolen. The Regent, starved of willing gifts for a century, accepts. Emotional beat: diplomacy as redemption.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The long winter breaks. Snowmelt floods the valleys; the kingdom grieves its dead and plants early. Alaric, restored, chooses exile over a throne built on his suffering. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah reckons what was lost: the childhood summer, the family name, pieces they can never recover—but stands whole anyway, with Wren filling some gaps with retold stories. Emotional beat: mourning and gratitude in one breath.

chapters.title: A New Map
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren publishes the true maps of the Thornfells, ending the smugglers' monopoly and the guild's power over people like Jonah. Emotional beat: knowledge as liberation.

chapters.title: The Taster Retires
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah tastes their last dish for the crown—freely, once, as a courtesy—and walks out of the palace without looking back. Emotional beat: laying down the armor of usefulness.

chapters.title: Spring, Chosen
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Jonah and Wren open a roadhouse at the foot of the Thornfells where travelers trade stories for supper. The prophecy book rests on a shelf, its last page blank. Emotional beat: a life written by choice, not fate.
